title: How are Opus 5.5's rates and how is GPT 6.1 Sol compared to it ?
author: SoonBlossom
selftext:
Hey y'all

For work reasons I'm currently using GPT 6.1 Sol and am very satisfied with it, I have the 20$ plan and since 6.1 Sol I can do tonnnn of things before I hit my weekly limit even in "very high" for the reasoning

But I see that everyone here seems to be using Opus 5.5and I was wondering :

For those of you who tryied both 6.1 Sol and Opus 5.5, what are the notable differences you can feel in game dev ? Is Opus 5.5 really that much better ?

And last question for everyone : how do you feel about Opus 5.5's rate ? Does it burn fast ? Do you feel you can do a lot of things with the 20$ plan (that's the one I would buy if I bought it

Thank you all !

(If you have any advices for the workflow feel free to tell, right now I'm using 6.1 Sol in very high reasoning with Godot and it's quite okay for what I do which is 2D pixel art games)

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body: I've been using SOL for quite some time, 5.6 was an excellent image pipeline, and 6.1 doesn't disappoint. Much tighter execution on the code passes as long as you properly structure the project.

replies.author: SoonBlossom
replies.body:
A thing that shocked me was the animations it can make

I generated a 2D pixel art of an octopus, I asked him to make an idle animation by telling him it's free to do what it wants as long as it respects the art direction and that the animation makes sense

It made a gif of 32 images of the octopus slightly breathing and moving a bit in idle mod

It feels insane to me, last time I tryied was 1 year ago and it used to do absolute "garbage" animations that weren't production ready

The one he did definitely is, it's consistant and looks nice, I'm really surprised

replies.author: ZymzAlchemy
replies.body:
Sprite sheets are your friend. Single render, (saves code) evenly spaced, slice and map in the code (or your art program of choice I prefer GIMP myself). 

https://preview.redd.it/6y8ajw8nh3th1.png?width=2032&format=png&auto=webp&s=a540d7b0ba6dedb5504ca8068680bd2d5407d1e5

replies.author: SoonBlossom
replies.body:
I used to ask sprite sheets too but every time I had inconsistencies between the images or the animation didn't make sense so this time I thought "fuck it" and went into work mode to ask him to do the whole animation, check if it looks good and iterate on it

It took like 10 minutes but the animation is perfect

I didn't try the sprite sheet thing in a long time so I'll try again ! Maybe it's better now !

replies.author: ZymzAlchemy
replies.body: YMMV but for me I make an 'art style guide' which tells SOL what I want the aesthetic to look like, then write up a prompt sheet that has a prompt for each asset sheet, the top of the sheet has guidelines for all the sheets size/spacing/resolution/number of cells and then I give the agent the two docs and if there is a character reference this and say something like 'execute 'sprite\_shopping\_list.md' against 'art\_guide.md' using provided reference <reference file>. 5.6 had some issues but 6.1 is noticeable better at consistency.

replies.author: SoonBlossom
replies.body:
I love the idea of this workflow, I'll give it a go !

I also work with .md files for the art direction and the general idea of the game so it knows what to do consistantly without me explaining each time, but I never thought about saving prompts to make sheets or sprites faster, I'll try that thanks for the tips !

replies.author: ZymzAlchemy
replies.body: I have a whole thing lol. I've been in this since the 80s with ASM so I'm all about never having too much documentation. ;)

comments.author: TomBombadilCannabico
comments.body:
I've been using codex since march. Coding and art wide it's decent, what annoys me is how the usage quotas got reduced over this time and how freaking slow the models are.

After all the hype I decided to try Opus 5.5 last week and wow. I didn't feel I had such a capable model with such a generous quota since at least june. Besides that it feels I'm running a faster astra high, that makes way less mistakes and besides that knows how to make UIs, my biggest problem.

replies.author: SoonBlossom
replies.body:
I was having stars in my eyes until the edit haha

Tho I'm about to say fuck it and just take a 20$ plan for Claude on top of my 20$ plan for GPT just to try it out and use Claude exclusively for games and keep GPT for work as I did

Honestly I feel like we can do so much with these AIs that 20$ feels dirt cheap, I hope it stays at that price for a long time hopefully (even tho I doubt it)

comments.author: TrickyPlastic
comments.body: Without the $200 plan opus is unusable. I can do loads of work with Sol 6.1 on a $20 plan.

comments.author: RageshAntony
comments.body: Can we generate animations in ChatGPT now ?

replies.author: SoonBlossom
replies.body:
Yeah, and very easily on top of that

You install the desktop application, you go into Codex, give it a 2D sprite and then you ask him the animation you want

I just asked him to do the idle animation of another sprite right now and to make sure the animation makes sense

It went alone for 16 minutes and came back with a 60 images gif of the animation, everything is fluid, consistant, and it looks good

Honestly I'm impressed

comments.author: 1Q49C
comments.body:
200$ plan user here, been using codex for almost a year. Recently jumped ship working on my project to opus 5.5, Astra and sol got nerfed hard. Opus has been incredible.

It not only understands what I want but we can pass ideas back and forth and they make sense, it’s just been the better model and I’ve only been using it for a week.

Astra and sol kept getting stuck in loops for experiments and documentation and when I updated documents to stop them from doing it.

Opus, is the way.

And the usage feels like the 20x plan I had for codex but I am only on the 100$ plan for Claude. Since I’m kind of done with my test run I’ll go to the 200$ plan now.

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body:
The frontier is constantly shifting between OpenAI and anthropics in locksteps. Just make your project and setup compatible with both, upgrade/downgrade one and the other subscription once new models are released.

With that being said, sol 6.1 doesn‘t feel like I really need to go back to OpenAI atm.
